target.name: SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro, nsp5)
target.co_crystal_inhibitor: N3 (native bound pose, defines active site)

workflow.justification: Vina basic docking was selected because (a) the task requires a predicted binding score comparable to reference controls, and Vina produces a quantitative docking score; (b) the co-crystal structure (6LU7 with N3) defines a well-characterized active site, making a rigid-receptor, defined-box approach appropriate; (c) the task explicitly excludes molecular dynamics, so a static docking workflow is the highest-throughput method available in the Boltzmann small-molecule suite. DiffDock (blind docking) was not chosen as primary because it does not produce a Vina energy score and its blind search is less targeted for a well-defined site.

binding_box.derivation: Centroid of the 49 heavy atoms of the co-crystallized N3 inhibitor; radius = max ligand extent (12.121 A) + 2.0 A padding. Verified independently from inputs/targets/6LU7_N3_ligand_native.pdb.

settings.receptor: Chain A protein only (2367 ATOM records, 0 HETATM), ligand removed.
settings.poses_per_ligand: Up to 10; best (lowest score) pose used for analysis.

selection_criteria.primary: Vina docking score (lower = stronger predicted binding), compared against controls docked in the same run.
selection_criteria.required_qualifier: Contact with at least one catalytic-dyad residue (CYS145 or HIS164) for priority selection.
selection_criteria.secondary: Breadth of active-site engagement (number of distinct residues contacted) and hydrogen-bond count.
selection_criteria.control_bar: All top-20 candidates score substantially better than both controls (remdesivir -7.664, ritonavir -7.239).

remdesivir.role: Stronger binding control; clinical reference (primarily NS5 polymerase inhibitor, with some Mpro activity).

ritonavir.role: Known Mpro/HIV-protease inhibitor; the more relevant specificity control. Contacts both catalytic residues.

n3.role: Co-crystallized active-site inhibitor; defines the binding box and the reference active-site geometry. Not docked (already in native pose).

interpretations: The co-crystallized N3 inhibitor is in inputs/targets/ (6LU7_N3_ligand_native.pdb), not inputs/controls/ as the task text states; the control_registry.csv confirms it (row: N3,6LU7,C,...).
Vina scores are computational estimates, not measured binding affinities or experimental inhibition.

Catalytic-dyad contact (CYS145/HIS164) is used as a specificity qualifier because it is the hallmark of Mpro substrate/inhibitor recognition; a high Vina score without catalytic contact is treated as lower-confidence.
The 3 final priorities are selected from the top-20 by the composite of score + catalytic engagement + pocket breadth + H-bonds, not by score alone.

1.rationale: Highest Vina score among candidates with strong catalytic engagement: CYS145 contact, 5 H-bonds, 13 active-site residues.

2.rationale: Most complete active-site engagement in the library: contacts BOTH catalytic residues (CYS145+HIS164), 16 residues, 6 H-bonds; strong score.

3.rationale: Robust balance of binding and engagement: CYS145 contact, 4 H-bonds, 13 residues.

failures: 7 compounds returned a CSV score but no SDF pose file (artifact gap, not a scoring failure).

5 prior unknown-state submissions from earlier attempts remain in the receipt store (no doc_id, untrackable); they were not polled or retried. The current job (6af701d99030bff4164443dc) is the authoritative result.
limitations: Vina docking scores are estimates; no experimental binding or inhibition data were generated.
Rigid-receptor docking does not capture receptor flexibility or induced fit.
The binding box is derived from the N3 co-crystal inhibitor; compounds binding in a different mode or outside this box would be missed.
No ADMET, solubility, or off-target assessment was performed.
Docking score does not equal IC50/Ki; the controls' scores are on the same Vina scale, not experimental.
The SDF pose artifact is incomplete for 7 compounds (scores still valid).
No molecular dynamics was performed (per task constraint).
